serverInfo.name: roc-syntax
serverInfo.description: Roc syntax, builtins, and language reference for the Zig-based compiler.

result.instructions: Roc language reference for the Zig-based compiler in roc-lang/roc (2026 nightlies). Before reading, writing, or reasoning about any Roc code, call `get_roc_syntax` once with no arguments. It returns the whole language and its builtins as two compact pages (~3.3k tokens), usually enough to finish the task without another call. Do this even when you believe you know Roc: the syntax changed with this compiler, so recalled Roc is unreliable (`Try` replaced `Result`, `value.method()` static dispatch is the normal style, and every builtin lives in one `Builtin.roc`). For details, use `get_roc_syntax(topic:)` for a worked example and the rules of one construct, `get_roc_module` for one module, and `roc_check` / `roc_fmt` to verify what you wrote. To find a Roc function or type, call `search_symbols`, and `search_project_symbols` for the `.roc` files of a project, before Grep. They return the whole signature with its docs, and one call takes up to 8 queries. Use Grep only when both find nothing. Name the platform in `scope` when the workspace has no app header yet: a project you are starting has no app header yet, so nothing but you knows which platform its code is for. Never request `Builtin.roc` whole. It is hundreds of thousands of tokens.

tools.name: get_roc_syntax
tools.title: Roc Overview and Syntax Topics (start here)
tools.description: Call with no arguments before reading, writing, or reasoning about any Roc code. It returns the whole language and its builtins: syntax, types, operator desugaring, modules, and where LLMs get Roc wrong. Call it even when you believe you know Roc: the Zig-based compiler changed the syntax. Pass `topic` for one construct: a worked example, its rules, and the errors it gives. Topics: idioms, iterators, ranges, record_fields, derived_methods, json, hashing, operators, pattern_matching, list_patterns, tag_unions, try_operator, strings, effects, loops, conditionals, tuples, records, types, compile_time, dict_set, memory, naming, numbers, opaque, nominal, functions, static_dispatch, imports, modules, packages, write_package, release_package, comments, testing, compiler, version_mismatch, app_header, dbg_crash, platforms, platform_abi, builder_pattern, scripting, error_design, joy_app, joy_http, joy_subscriptions, ray_project, ray_game, ray_app, ray_draw, ray_input, ray_tasks, ray_text, ray_assets, release_multiplatform_ray, wasm_bridge_ray, ray_headless, pixel_canvas_ray, ray_capture, parser_combinators, parser_csv, parser_yaml, parser_json, parser_xml, parser_markdown, parser_asciidoc, parser_roc_syntax, parser_http, parser_compile_time, random_generators, html_views, html_ssr, weaver_cli, weaver_builder, weaver_options, weaver_subcommands, weaver_raw_args.

topic.description: Omit for the overview. A topic name (e.g. 'pattern_matching'), a package name for its page (e.g. 'roc-parser'), an example (e.g. 'basic-cli/hello'), or a question, which gets pointers when no topic is a sure match.

scope.description: One corpus only. Without `topic`, returns the page of that corpus. Omit for the language and builtins, or name a platform for its API. With `topic`, searches only the topics of that corpus. Name a platform (basic-webserver, basic-cli, joy, roc-ray) for what a host provides, such as I/O, graphics or networking, rather than the language or the builtins.

tools.name: list_roc_index
tools.title: List What the Other Roc Tools Accept
tools.description: What the other tools accept. `scopes`: the corpora `scope` takes, and documented packages. `topics`: the topics `get_roc_syntax` takes. `modules`: the module paths `get_roc_module` takes. `examples`: worked programs.

scope.description: For kind='topics', 'modules', 'examples': one corpus only. Omit for the working set.

tools.name: search_symbols
tools.title: Search Symbols by Name or Type
tools.description: Find builtins and platform APIs by name, by type, or both, written as a Roc annotation `name : Type`. A name (`concat`, `Str.concat`) returns each exact match with its docs, else the names that contain it. A type (`: Str`, or anything with `->`) is a structural search: a type variable matches any type, `-> T` matches the return type, `T ->` the arguments, and argument order matters. Both, as in `ceil : -> Dec`, lists the names that contain `ceil`, ranked by type.

query.description: Up to 8 queries. Each is a name ('Str.concat'), words in a name ('size window'), a module ending in '.' ('Keys.'), a type ('-> Bool', or 'Frame ->' for the functions that take a Frame), or a name and a type ('ceil : -> Dec').

scope.description: A platform to read in place of the one this app's header imports, or one corpus to limit a list to. Name a platform (basic-webserver, basic-cli, joy, roc-ray) for what a host provides, such as I/O, graphics or networking, rather than the language or the builtins.

limit.description: Max list entries per query (default 10, or 5 for several queries).

tools.name: get_roc_module
tools.title: Get a Roc Module
tools.description: Every function and type in one module as a signature list: a builtin (`Str`, `U64`), a module of the app's platform (`Path`), or a module of a documented package (`Html`). Bare `U64` resolves to `Num.U64`. detail='full' adds docstrings and examples. For one function use `search_symbols`. For a module of your project, read its file.

detail.description: 'signatures' (default) lists name and type only. 'full' adds docstrings and examples, ~5x longer.

scope.description: Read a platform other than the one this app's header imports. Rarely needed.

tools.name: roc_check
tools.title: Type-check Roc source with `roc check`
tools.description: Type-check Roc source with the real compiler. Pass `code` or `path`. Requires the Roc compiler.

code.description: Roc source to check. Not with `path`.

path.description: Absolute path to a .roc file. Not with `code`.

scope.description: Wrap headerless `code` in this platform's app. Omit if it has a header.

tools.name: roc_fmt
tools.title: Format Roc source with `roc fmt`
tools.description: Format Roc source. Pass `code` or `path`, the same either/or as `roc_check`. Never writes the file. Requires the Roc compiler.

code.description: Roc source to format. Not with `path`.

path.description: Absolute path to a .roc file. Not with `code`.

tools.name: search_project_symbols
tools.title: Search in Codebase by Name or Type
tools.description: `search_symbols` over the `.roc` files of your project or other codebase.

root.description: Root of the codebase, absolute. The workspace by default.

resourceTemplates.name: roc-topic
resourceTemplates.title: Roc Syntax Topic
resourceTemplates.description: Per-topic Roc syntax snippet. Use the URI roc-syntax://topic/<name> with one of the registered topic names.

resourceTemplates.name: roc-platform-example
resourceTemplates.title: Platform Example Program
resourceTemplates.description: One complete, compiling program from a platform's example set. Every bundled example passes `roc check` against the pinned platform. Use roc-syntax://platform/{basic-webserver|basic-cli|joy|roc-ray}/example/<name>, and list_roc_index with kind='examples' for the names.

resourceTemplates.name: roc-package-page
resourceTemplates.title: Package Page
resourceTemplates.description: What a documented package is for, its topics and examples, and whether this app pins it.

resourceTemplates.name: roc-package-example
resourceTemplates.title: Package Example Program
resourceTemplates.description: One complete, compiling program from a documented package's example set. list_roc_index with kind='examples' names them.

resourceTemplates.name: roc-platform-doc
resourceTemplates.title: Platform Documentation Page
resourceTemplates.description: A prose page shipped by a platform, bundled unchanged from its pinned release. Use roc-syntax://platform/basic-webserver/doc/<name>, e.g. .../doc/sse. basic-cli ships no prose pages.

resources.name: roc-overview
resources.title: Roc Overview (start here)
resources.description: The whole Roc language and its builtins in two compact pages (~3k tokens). Read this before any other resource in this server. The other resources give the details that it names.

resources.name: roc-syntax-reference
resources.title: Roc Syntax Reference
resources.description: Mirror of roc-lang/roc's all_syntax_test.roc. It demonstrates every Roc language construct in the new compiler.

resources.name: roc-builtin
resources.title: Roc Builtin Index
resources.description: Index of every builtin module and its method count. Builtin.roc itself is hundreds of thousands of tokens, so use get_roc_module or search_symbols, and do not read it whole.

resources.title: idioms
resources.description: Which construct to use when several would work: anonymous tag unions for errors, structural before nominal, derive before hand-write, chains before pipes.
resources.name: roc-topic-idioms

resources.title: iterators
resources.description: `Iter` (pure) and `Stream` (effectful) iterators, the `iter`/`next` methods behind `for ... in`, `for!` over a `Stream`, and the adapters.
resources.name: roc-topic-iterators

resources.title: ranges
resources.description: Range operators `..<` and `..=`, the `Range(num)` value, `step_by`, `iter_rev`, and custom numeric ranges.
resources.name: roc-topic-ranges

resources.title: record_fields
resources.description: Defaulted (`field : Type ?? default`) and optional (`field ?: Type`) record fields, `.?field` reads, and the `..rest` pattern.
resources.name: roc-topic-record_fields

resources.title: derived_methods
resources.description: The `method : _` compiler-derived opt-in, the full well-known-method table, and the literal-conversion hooks.
resources.name: roc-topic-derived_methods

resources.title: json
resources.description: `Json` (`Encoding.Json`) parse/encode, the `parser_for`/`encoder_for` codec protocol, its `Encodable`/`Parseable` where aliases, the `Default`/`CamelCase`/`TrailingCommas` dialects, and missing fields.
resources.name: roc-topic-json

resources.title: hashing
resources.description: `to_hash` and the `Hasher.write_*` methods, plus `Crypto.SHA256`/`Crypto.BLAKE3` digests.
resources.name: roc-topic-hashing

resources.title: operators
resources.description: Arithmetic, comparison, boolean, range (`..<`/`..=`), and `??` operators, with their method desugaring.
resources.name: roc-topic-operators

resources.title: pattern_matching
resources.description: `match` expressions: alternatives, guards, literal and code-point patterns, `as`, exhaustiveness and redundancy, destructuring, string captures.
resources.name: roc-topic-pattern_matching

resources.title: list_patterns
resources.description: List destructuring with `..`, `as` bindings, and match guards.
resources.name: roc-topic-list_patterns

resources.title: tag_unions
resources.description: Tag unions, nominal `Try`, multi-payload tags, open unions and `..others` pass-through, qualified tags, nominal vs structural tags, and the empty union `[]`.
resources.name: roc-topic-tag_unions

resources.title: try_operator
resources.description: The `?` postfix operator for short-circuiting on `Err`, including err mapping.
resources.name: roc-topic-try_operator

resources.title: strings
resources.description: String literals, interpolation `${...}`, multi-line `\\`, unicode escapes, UTF-8 conversion, `Str.len`, single-quote code points, equality without normalization, and bidi controls.
resources.name: roc-topic-strings

resources.title: effects
resources.description: Effectful functions (`!` suffix, `=>` arrow), purity inference, the errors and the warning for wrong purity, and the `!` twins of higher-order builtins. `echo!` is built-in and appends no newline.
resources.name: roc-topic-effects

resources.title: loops
resources.description: For loops, while loops, `break`, reassignable `var $name`, exhaustive `for` patterns, and the unused value that a loop body cannot drop.
resources.name: roc-topic-loops

resources.title: conditionals
resources.description: `if`/`else`/`else if` expressions, the one-line `if (cond) a else b`. `else` is optional when the body is `{}`. Short-circuiting `and`/`or`.
resources.name: roc-topic-conditionals

resources.title: tuples
resources.description: Tuples, destructuring, `.0`/`.1` index access, pattern matching.
resources.name: roc-topic-tuples

resources.title: records
resources.description: Record literals, puns, field access, record patterns, `{ ..base, ... }` update and its limits, and open records.
resources.name: roc-topic-records

resources.title: types
resources.description: Type annotations, type variables (`_`, `_elem`), generalization, `where` clauses and `where` aliases, `Thing : thing`, rank-1 and no-HKT limits, aliases, and recursive types.
resources.name: roc-topic-types

resources.title: compile_time
resources.description: Compile-time evaluation of top-level constants and pure calls, compile-time crashes as compile errors, no effects at build time, empty collections, binary size, and code with errors.
resources.name: roc-topic-compile_time

resources.title: dict_set
resources.description: `Dict` and `Set`: building them with `empty`/`single`/`from_list`, `get` with `??`, `insert`/`remove`/`update`, insertion-order iteration and how `remove` changes it, set operations, and what a key type needs.
resources.name: roc-topic-dict_set

resources.title: memory
resources.description: Immutable values, reference counting, opportunistic in-place updates (`List.set`), no pointers or value identity, no reference cycles.
resources.name: roc-topic-memory

resources.title: naming
resources.description: Naming rules for values, types and `var`s, reserved words, definition order, unused-name warnings, shadowing and duplicate definitions, a type named after a builtin, and the `var` rules: capture, and the update that only `=` makes.
resources.name: roc-topic-naming

resources.title: numbers
resources.description: Numeric types and literals (`5.U64`, `0x5`, `1.5e-2`, underscores), `Dec` versus floats, literal defaulting, and custom number types through `from_numeral` and `Numeral`.
resources.name: roc-topic-numbers

resources.title: opaque
resources.description: Opaque types (`::`) hide the representation. Methods are optional.
resources.name: roc-topic-opaque

resources.title: nominal
resources.description: Distinct nominal types (`:=`), explicit construction and destructuring (`T.(v)`, `T.{...}`), when literals lift, and associated constants.
resources.name: roc-topic-nominal

resources.title: functions
resources.description: Function literals `|args| body`, blocks, `return` and the unreachable code after it, `...`, recursion, top-level cycles, and tail calls (accumulators, modulo cons).
resources.name: roc-topic-functions

resources.title: static_dispatch
resources.description: `.method()` static dispatch, calling a function stored in a record field, the `|>` pipe operator, and well-known methods.
resources.name: roc-topic-static_dispatch

resources.title: imports
resources.description: Module imports, aliases (`as`), file embedding (`import "x" as y : Str` or `List(U8)`), and mutually recursive types in a void module.
resources.name: roc-topic-imports

resources.title: modules
resources.description: Type modules (one nominal type per file, named like the file), what a module hides, nested types (`Url.ParseErr`), void modules (`Util :: [].{ ... }`), no import cycles, and the four module kinds and their headers.
resources.name: roc-topic-modules

resources.title: packages
resources.description: Package headers and dependencies: `package [...] { ... }`, URL (`.tar.zst`, hash) and path packages, version resolution, shorthands, platform-specific packages, and nominal type identity across packages.
resources.name: roc-topic-packages

resources.title: write_package
resources.description: Set up or revise a Roc package repo: a checklist, the `src/` layout, and every file of a small package as a snippet: `src/main.roc`, a documented type module with `expect`s, a hidden module, an example, `scripts/all_tests.sh`, `.gitignore`.
resources.name: roc-topic-write_package

resources.title: release_package
resources.description: Ship a Roc package: a checklist, then `.roc-version` and setup-roc, `scripts/bundle.sh`, a bundle test over localhost with `--replace-dep`, `tests.yaml` on 5 runners, version rules and `roc bump`, `release.yml` with roc-lang/release-package, docs on GitHub Pages, compiler-update PRs, and repo settings.
resources.name: roc-topic-release_package

resources.title: comments
resources.description: Comments: `#`, `##` doc comments in Markdown, code blocks and `[Name]` autolinks in docs, `roc docs`, shebang lines, and the ban on bidirectional controls.
resources.name: roc-topic-comments

resources.title: testing
resources.description: Testing with `expect`, multi-line `expect { ... }` blocks, inline assertions, `?` inside `expect`, and the control flow rules inside `expect`.
resources.name: roc-topic-testing

resources.title: compiler
resources.description: The `roc` command line: check, test, run and build, exit codes, `--opt` levels and their per-command defaults, `--target`, `fmt`, `deps` with `--replace-dep`, `docs`, `bundle`, `bump`, and `roc glue`.
resources.name: roc-topic-compiler

resources.title: version_mismatch
resources.description: A released platform or package does not compile: find the file of the error, read the nightly of the release from its repo, switch the compiler, choose one nightly for the build, and when to stop.
resources.name: roc-topic-version_mismatch

resources.title: app_header
resources.description: Headerless apps and `app [main!] { pf: platform "..." }` declarations.
resources.name: roc-topic-app_header

resources.title: dbg_crash
resources.description: `dbg` output (stderr, `to_inspect`, compile time), `crash`, and the planned `continue`.
resources.name: roc-topic-dbg_crash

resources.title: platforms
resources.description: Writing/maintaining a Roc platform: platform header, `requires` forms, reserved `roc__` symbols, `main_for_host!`, hosted FFI (wrapper and host-direct forms) and its rules, `output: Archive`, a platform with no effects, and the host side with its runtime hooks. The ABI edge cases are in `platform_abi`.
resources.name: roc-topic-platforms

resources.title: platform_abi
resources.description: The host ABI of a platform: closed hosted results, the single-tag discriminant byte, record field order and `_ : {}`, three-state returns, the `()` unit argument, the representations of `Path`, a shared `IOErr`, and who frees a hosted argument.
resources.name: roc-topic-platform_abi

resources.title: builder_pattern
resources.description: The fluent/builder pattern: nominal record type + setter methods that take and return Self. Terminal `!` executors. Used by basic-cli's `Cmd`. Also record builders, `{ ... }.Type` over `map2`.
resources.name: roc-topic-builder_pattern

resources.title: scripting
resources.description: Writing and running a standalone .roc utility script: how `roc run`/`test`/`build`/`bundle` and a `#!` line reach it, argument dispatch to exit code, CSV and YAML into records and ad-hoc parsing with `lukewilliamboswell/roc-parser`, stdin pipelines, and the one place errors become messages. Assumes basic-cli.
resources.name: roc-topic-scripting

resources.title: error_design
resources.description: Designing error tag unions: anonymous over declared, structured record payloads, per-subsystem wrappers (`StdoutErr(IOErr)`), open `[..]` for composability, `?` vs `? Tag` vs `.map_err`.
resources.name: roc-topic-error_design

resources.title: webserver_handler
resources.description: The basic-webserver request handler: `init!`/`respond!`/`shutdown!`, routing on method and target, reading the streaming body, and the four `Server.Outcome` constructors.
resources.name: roc-topic-webserver_handler

resources.title: webserver_sqlite
resources.description: SQLite from a request handler: open the pool in `init!`, `query_many!` with derived row codecs, `execute!` writes, transactions, and prepared statements.
resources.name: roc-topic-webserver_sqlite

resources.title: webserver_sse
resources.description: Server-sent events: `Server.stream` over an `Sse.unfold!` state machine, the `Emit`/`Wait`/`End` step, wake scheduling, and named events with ids and retry.
resources.name: roc-topic-webserver_sse

resources.title: webserver_html
resources.description: Server-rendered HTML with `Html` and `Attribute`: escaped text by default, `element`/`void_element` for tags without helpers, and the one unescaped-HTML call.
resources.name: roc-topic-webserver_html

resources.title: webserver_forms
resources.description: Form bodies: `parse_form_url_encoded` into a `Dict`, and `parse_multipart_form_data` into raw parts with their disposition and content type.
resources.name: roc-topic-webserver_forms

resources.title: webserver_static
resources.description: Serving files: `FileRoot` and `RelativeFile`, native routes the host answers without entering Roc, and `file_response_with` for a transfer Roc authorized.
resources.name: roc-topic-webserver_static

resources.title: cli_app
resources.description: The basic-cli application contract: `main!`, the `List(OsStr)` arguments, `Err(Exit(code))`, and turning error tags into messages at the edge.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_app

resources.title: cli_files
resources.description: Files and directories through `Path`: whole-file reads and writes, metadata, `PathErr` matching, directory trees, and the buffered `File.Reader`.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_files

resources.title: cli_command
resources.description: Running other programs: `Cmd.exec!`, the chained `Cmd` builder, captured output, a controlled environment, and exit codes.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_command

resources.title: cli_http
resources.description: The HTTP client: `Http.get_utf8!`, `Http.send!`, JSON through `get!`/`send_json!`/`decode_json_response`, and the `roc-lang/http` request and response types.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_http

resources.title: cli_sqlite
resources.description: SQLite: `execute!` writes, `query!` and `query_many!` reads, hand-built row decoders, prepared statements, and the `Binding` value type.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_sqlite

resources.title: cli_terminal
resources.description: Standard streams, raw mode, and the small effects around them: `Stdin`/`Stdout`/`Stderr`, `Tty`, `Env`, `Utc`, `Sleep`, `Random`, `Locale`.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_terminal

resources.title: cli_net
resources.description: TCP streams and URL parsing: `Tcp.connect!`, the four reads and their per-call timeouts, and `Url.parse` with its accessors and relative resolution.
resources.name: roc-topic-cli_net

resources.title: joy_app
resources.description: The shape of a Joy app: the four required functions and the Model and Msg types, the flags init receives, effects as data, callbacks as lambdas, a component mapped with Html.map and Effect.map, and a test of what update returns.
resources.name: roc-topic-joy_app

resources.title: joy_http
resources.description: HTTP from a Joy app: Http.get, Http.request from default_request with headers, a JSON body and a timeout, why a 404 is Ok, matching HttpErr, and a test that answers a request as the host does.
resources.name: roc-topic-joy_http

resources.title: joy_subscriptions
resources.description: Keyboard, intervals, URL changes and JavaScript ports in Joy: which are subscriptions and which are effects, timer units, Sub.KeyEvent, debouncing, and switching a subscription off.
resources.name: roc-topic-joy_subscriptions

resources.title: ray_project
resources.description: Starting a RocRay project: the opaque `App.Config` and its receivers, frame pacing, declared permissions, argv-aware startup with `App.init_for_args`, assets from the source tree or beside the executable, the default Escape exit key, and seeding a generator.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_project

resources.title: ray_game
resources.description: How a game is put together here: resources beside the world in the model, a pure step taking seconds of delta, cues performed at the edge, a state tag driving `update!`, and derived values kept out of the model.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_game

resources.title: ray_app
resources.description: The RocRay application contract: `init!`/`update!`/`render!`, the required `Model` and `Msg`, `App.init`, `update!`'s `App.Io` argument, exiting with `Err(Exit(code))`, and error sets with no `..` in return position.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_app

resources.title: ray_draw
resources.description: Drawing through `Draw.Frame`: the styles, shapes, convex polygons and concave shapes split into triangles, scoped camera and scissor callbacks, and listing `ScopeLimit` in `render!`'s error set.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_draw

resources.title: ray_input
resources.description: One device snapshot per cycle: held against pressed, text entry as codepoints, mouse position and wheel deltas, gamepads resolved out of the snapshot, and the clipboard.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_input

resources.title: ray_tasks
resources.description: Work that waits: `Task.spawn!` with the input as its witness, services from `App.Io` captured by the closure, directory handles, one message per task on a later `input.messages`, and the phase rule the types do not carry.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_tasks

resources.title: ray_text
resources.description: Text three ways: `Text.from(str, font).prepare!()` measured once outside `render!` and drawn many times, a builder drawn directly, and `frame.text_at!` for debug text.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_text

resources.title: ray_assets
resources.description: Assets: a store opened on a `Files.ReadDir`, textures and sounds loaded through it, reference-counted handles kept in the model, generated textures, sound effects made in code with `Audio.gen_sound!` and played at a varied pitch, and sprite sheets and animation.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_assets

resources.title: release_multiplatform_ray
resources.description: Shipping a RocRay app to other systems: `roc build --target=` for x64mac, arm64mac, x64v1glibc and x64win, what builds from Linux, the Wayland bundle, one zip per system with assets and licenses, and unsigned-binary warnings.
resources.name: roc-topic-release_multiplatform_ray

resources.title: wasm_bridge_ray
resources.description: Bringing a RocRay game to the browser: a platform-free core (model, advance, frame as a list of shapes) driven by a roc-ray runner and by a custom wasm32 platform with `exports:`, a host built separately, `roc glue`, and the JavaScript frame loop.
resources.name: roc-topic-wasm_bridge_ray

resources.title: ray_headless
resources.description: Running an app with no person at the keyboard, in CI or as a smoke test of a cross-built executable on its target: the `--host-` switches (`--host-headless-frames=N`, `--host-keys`, `--host-close`), what the app's argv and Capture see, and the exit codes a CI job reads.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_headless

resources.title: pixel_canvas_ray
resources.description: A pixel-art look on a fixed low-resolution canvas: a `Draw.RenderTexture` loaded once, the scene drawn into it with `with_render_texture!`, scaled up by the largest whole number with bars at the edges, sharp pixels with the `Point` filter, and the mouse mapped to canvas pixels.
resources.name: roc-topic-pixel_canvas_ray

resources.title: ray_capture
resources.description: Capturing the app's own frames: `with_output_dir`, a PNG screenshot from a task, `screenshot_texture!` for a PNG at another size, a GIF or WebM recording from `Capture.default` watched in `input.capture`, `pixel_at!` and `read_region!` for a pixel test, and the phase each call needs.
resources.name: roc-topic-ray_capture

resources.title: parser_combinators
resources.description: A parser for your own text format with roc-parser: Parser.const with keep and skip, one_of, many, sep_by, maybe, and_then, Parser.lazy for recursion, and Utf8.parse_str against parse_str_partial.
resources.name: roc-topic-parser_combinators

resources.title: parser_csv
resources.description: CSV into your own record type with roc-parser: CSV.parse and MissingRequiredField(Str), optional and empty columns, parse_normalized, parse_headerless into tuples, and parse_with for a hand-built row.
resources.name: roc-topic-parser_csv

resources.title: parser_yaml
resources.description: A YAML config with roc-parser: Yaml.decode into a record, Try(_, [Missing]) and Try(_, [Null]) fields, Yaml.decoder with KebabCase and Reject, or a tree with parse_str, get_path and as_str, or Yaml.tokenize_str to highlight source.
